speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. Also, have you noticed any other symptoms like hearing loss, tinnitus, double vision, or difficulty speaking?

speaker: Patient
text: 59-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with a sudden-onset sensation that the room is spinning, leading to several episodes of nausea and vomiting. The symptoms started as he was going to bed and lasted for approximately 3 minutes. He mentions that he has never experienced anything like this before and currently feels at his baseline.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That sudden spinning sensation lasting only 3 minutes is very suggestive of a specific type of inner ear issue. Since you feel back to your baseline now, have you noticed any ringing in your ears, a feeling of fullness, or any hearing changes in recent days?

text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV). The clinical presentation of sudden, brief (3 minutes) spinning vertigo that resolves completely is the classic definition of BPPV. The recent normal audiometry and MRI results rule out Meniere's disease, vestibular neuritis, and central causes like stroke or tumor, confirming a peripheral mechanical etiology.
